# IgFold Model Architecture



The IgFold model architecture represents a sophisticated deep learning system specifically designed for antibody structure prediction. Built on the principles of Invariant Point Attention (IPA) and Graph Transformers, the model transforms sequence embeddings into accurate 3D atomic coordinates through a carefully orchestrated three-stage pipeline. This architecture achieves high-accuracy predictions while maintaining computational efficiency, enabling rapid structure generation for massive antibody datasets.

## Core Design Philosophy

IgFold's architecture embodies a **sequence-to-structure transformation pipeline** that leverages both evolutionary information (from pretrained protein language models) and geometric constraints specific to antibody molecules. The design centers on three fundamental principles: **rotational invariance** for 3D coordinate prediction, **pairwise representation learning** for capturing inter-residue relationships, and **modular processing stages** that progressively refine structural representations. The model operates on a fixed 4-atom representation per residue (N, CA, C, O backbone atoms), enabling consistent output formats suitable for downstream structural analysis.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L19-L48), [interface.py](igfold/model/interface.py#L6-L40)

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Input["Input Stage"]
        A[Sequence Embeddings<br/>512-dim BERT features] --> B[Attention Maps<br/>64-dim pairwise]
        C[Template Coordinates<br/>Optional] --> D[Transformations]
    end
    
    subgraph Transform["Feature Transformation"]
        E[Node Transform<br/>Linear → ReLU → LayerNorm] --> F[Edge Transform<br/>Linear → ReLU → LayerNorm]
        A --> E
        B --> F
    end
    
    subgraph Main["Main Processing Block"]
        F --> G[GraphTransformer<br/>Multi-head attention on nodes]
        G --> H[TriangleMultiplicative<br/>Outgoing & Incoming]
        H --> I[Iterative Updates<br/>Depth layers]
        E --> G
    end
    
    subgraph IPA["Invariant Point Attention Stages"]
        I --> J[Template IPA<br/>Integrate template info]
        J --> K[Structure IPA<br/>De novo prediction]
        D --> J
        K --> L[Deviation Head<br/>pRMSD prediction]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output Generation"]
        K --> M[3D Coordinates<br/>4 atoms × 3D per residue]
        L --> N[pRMSD Estimates<br/>Per-residue confidence]
    end
    
    style Input fill:#e3f2fd
    style IPA fill:#fff3e0
    style Output fill:#e8f5e9
```

The model processes input through **five major computational stages**, each with distinct responsibilities. The input transformation stage adapts pretrained embeddings to the model's internal dimensionality, followed by iterative refinement through the TriangleGraphTransformer block. Template information integration (when available) occurs through the template IPA module, while the structure IPA module performs the primary coordinate prediction task. The deviation head provides confidence estimates for each predicted residue, enabling quality assessment without requiring experimental structures.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L196-L370), [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L8-L45)

## Component Architecture Details

### Input Representation Layer

The **feature transformation layer** converts pretrained BERT embeddings into the model's working representation space. BERT features (512-dimensional) pass through a three-stage transformation pipeline: linear projection to node dimension, ReLU activation, and layer normalization. Simultaneously, attention maps (64-dimensional) undergo similar transformation to produce edge representations. This dual-pathway design ensures that both sequence-level features (nodes) and pairwise relationships (edges) are appropriately scaled for subsequent processing.

```python
self.str_node_transform = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(512, self.node_dim),  # Feature dimension reduction
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.LayerNorm(self.node_dim),
)
self.str_edge_transform = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(64, self.node_dim),   # Attention map expansion
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.LayerNorm(self.node_dim),
)
```

The node dimension is configurable but typically set to accommodate the complexity of antibody structures. These transformed representations form the foundation for the graph-based processing that follows.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L50-L65)

### Main TriangleGraphTransformer Block

The **TriangleGraphTransformer** represents the core innovation in IgFold's architecture, combining two complementary mechanisms for capturing both **node-node interactions** and **edge-edge relationships**. Each layer consists of three components executed sequentially: a GraphTransformer for updating node representations based on edge information, an outgoing triangle multiplicative module for capturing edge relationships in one direction, and an incoming triangle multiplicative module for the opposite direction.

| Component | Primary Function | Input | Output |
|-----------|------------------|-------|--------|
| GraphTransformer | Node aggregation using edges | Nodes, Edges | Updated nodes |
| Triangle Outgoing | Edge-outgoing edge relationships | Edges | Edge updates |
| Triangle Incoming | Edge-incoming edge relationships | Edges | Edge updates |

This architecture enables the model to learn **rich pairwise representations** that capture geometric constraints essential for accurate structure prediction. The iterative nature (configurable depth) allows progressive refinement of both node and edge features.

Sources: [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L9-L45)

> [!TIP]
> The TriangleMultiplicativeModule implements **axial attention** over edge representations, enabling efficient O(N²) processing of pairwise relationships. This is critical for capturing the geometric constraints that define protein backbone conformations without incurring O(N³) complexity associated with full 3D graph operations.

### Invariant Point Attention (IPA) Modules

The **IPA architecture** comprises two specialized instances serving different purposes: the Template IPA (IPAEncoder) and Structure IPA (IPATransformer). Both modules leverage **Invariant Point Attention**, a mechanism that performs attention operations in a rotationally invariant space, making them ideal for 3D structure prediction tasks.

The **Template IPA** integrates structural information from homologous templates when available. It operates on node representations from the main block, combining them with pairwise edge representations and template coordinates (expressed as rotations and translations). This enables the model to leverage evolutionary structural information while maintaining the ability to predict de novo structures when templates are unavailable.

The **Structure IPA** performs the primary coordinate prediction task. Starting from the refined node representations, it iteratively updates both the internal representation space and the 3D coordinates through alternating attention and coordinate update steps. The module outputs both atomic coordinates (4 atoms per residue: N, CA, C, O) and the frame transformations (translations and rotations) used during prediction.

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L34-L248), [IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py#L16-L175)

### Deviation Prediction Head

The **deviation prediction head** provides per-residue quality estimates in the form of predicted RMSD (pRMSD) values. This auxiliary task runs parallel to coordinate prediction, taking a separate pathway through the feature space. Deviation nodes pass through their own transformation layers, undergo IPA processing using the structure predictions (with detached gradients to prevent feedback), and ultimately produce 4-dimensional outputs per residue representing confidence estimates. These values correlate with the expected structural accuracy, enabling users to identify potentially unreliable regions in predictions.

```python
dev_nodes = self.dev_node_transform(bert_feats)
dev_edges = self.dev_edge_transform(bert_attn)
dev_out_feats = self.dev_ipa(
    dev_nodes,
    translations=ipa_translations.detach(),  # Prevent gradient flow
    rotations=ipa_rotations.detach(),
    pairwise_repr=dev_edges,
)
dev_pred = F.relu(self.dev_linear(dev_out_feats))  # 4D per residue
```

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L90-L112), [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L265-L275)

## Configuration and Parameters

The model architecture is highly configurable through a configuration dictionary, enabling adaptation to different computational budgets and accuracy requirements. Key parameters control the dimensionality of representations and the depth of processing stages.

| Parameter | Description | Typical Value |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| `node_dim` | Internal node/edge dimensionality | 256 |
| `depth` | TriangleGraphTransformer layers | 4-8 |
| `gt_depth` | GraphTransformer depth per layer | 1 |
| `gt_heads` | GraphTransformer attention heads | 8 |
| `temp_ipa_depth` | Template IPA layers | 4 |
| `str_ipa_depth` | Structure IPA layers | 4 |
| `dev_ipa_depth` | Deviation head IPA layers | 4 |

The modular design allows **trade-offs between accuracy and speed**—shallower networks reduce computation time while deeper networks capture more complex structural patterns. All IPA modules use multiple attention heads (typically 8) to capture diverse geometric relationships.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L35-L48)

## Data Flow and Processing Pipeline

The forward pass executes a carefully orchestrated sequence of transformations:

1. **Input preparation**: Sequence embeddings and attention maps are concatenated from multiple chains, template coordinates are processed into rotation/translation representations, and batch masks are constructed for multi-chain processing.

2. **Feature transformation**: BERT features and attentions are projected to the model's working dimensionality through node and edge transforms.

3. **Graph refinement**: The TriangleGraphTransformer iteratively refines node and edge representations through alternating GraphTransformer and triangle multiplicative operations.

4. **Template integration**: If templates are available, the Template IPA incorporates structural information while maintaining geometric consistency.

5. **Coordinate prediction**: The Structure IPA generates 3D coordinates through iterative updates, producing both atom positions and frame transformations.

6. **Quality estimation**: The deviation head generates confidence scores based on the predicted structure.

7. **Output assembly**: Predicted coordinates, confidence estimates, and optional intermediate embeddings are packaged into an `IgFoldOutput` object for downstream use.

The pipeline maintains **rotational and translational invariance** throughout, ensuring that predictions depend only on the intrinsic structure of the antibody rather than its absolute position or orientation in space.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L196-L370), [interface.py](igfold/model/interface.py#L22-L40)

> [!TIP]
> The model uses a **4-atom backbone representation** (N, CA, C, O atoms) rather than full atomic coordinates. This design choice reduces computational complexity while preserving the essential geometric information needed for antibody structure determination, enabling predictions that are both accurate and computationally efficient.

## Architectural Innovations

IgFold introduces several key architectural innovations that distinguish it from general protein structure prediction models:

**Triangular update mechanisms** capture the multi-scale nature of protein folding by considering both residue-residue interactions (through GraphTransformer) and relationship relationships (through TriangleMultiplicativeModule). This dual-level attention enables the model to learn **hierarchical geometric constraints** critical for antibody structure.

**Decomposed IPA stages** separate template integration from de novo prediction, allowing the model to leverage evolutionary information when available while maintaining strong performance on novel sequences. The three-stage pipeline (main block → template IPA → structure IPA) enables **progressive refinement** of structural hypotheses.

**Parallel confidence prediction** provides immediate quality assessment without requiring additional structural analyses or comparison to experimental structures. The deviation head learns to predict per-residue accuracy, enabling users to identify reliable regions for downstream applications.

These innovations collectively enable IgFold to achieve **high accuracy predictions** (median backbone RMSD < 1.0 Å) while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for large-scale antibody library analysis.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L67-L88), [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L8-L45)

## Next Steps

To deepen your understanding of the IgFold architecture, explore the detailed mechanisms of its key components:

- Learn about the **Graph Transformer components** that enable efficient node and edge representation learning in [Graph Transformer Components](7-graph-transformer-components)

- Dive into the **Invariant Point Attention** mechanism that enables rotationally invariant 3D coordinate prediction in [Invariant Point Attention (IPA) Implementation](8-invariant-point-attention-ipa-implementation)

- Understand how **sequence embeddings are generated** and transformed for model input in [Sequence Input and Embedding Pipeline](9-sequence-input-and-embedding-pipeline)

- Examine the complete **forward pass implementation** and coordinate generation process in [IgFold Model Forward Pass](23-igfold-model-forward-pass)

# Graph Transformer Components



The graph transformer architecture in IgFold represents a sophisticated integration of node-based and edge-based attention mechanisms, specifically designed to capture both local and long-range interactions in antibody sequences. These components form the core feature extraction pipeline that processes BERT embeddings before structure prediction via Invariant Point Attention (IPA). The architecture combines three specialized components: a graph attention mechanism for node-wise information aggregation, a triangle multiplicative module for edge-wise updates, and a transformer that orchestrates their interactions.

## Graph Transformer Architecture

The GraphTransformer implements a multi-head attention mechanism that operates on graph-structured data, where nodes represent residues and edges represent pairwise relationships between residues. Unlike standard transformers, this architecture explicitly incorporates edge features into the attention computation through the Attention class [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L70-L178). The architecture consists of stacked layers, each containing attention and optional feedforward blocks [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L187-L255).

The attention mechanism follows a standard query-key-value pattern with edge augmentation. Queries, keys, and values are projected from node representations, while edge representations are projected and added to keys and values [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L106-L131). This edge-aware design allows pairwise relationships (such as coevolutionary signals or distance potentials) to directly influence attention weights.

The following diagram illustrates the data flow through a single GraphTransformer layer:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Input["Input"]
        nodes["Node Representations<br/>(batch × seq_len × dim)"]
        edges["Edge Representations<br/>(batch × seq_len × seq_len × edge_dim)"]
    end
    
    subgraph Attention["Attention Block"]
        to_q["Project to Q"]
        to_kv["Project to K,V"]
        edge_kv["Project edges"]
        add["Add edge info to K,V"]
        sim["Compute similarity<br/>Q @ K × scale"]
        mask["Apply optional mask"]
        softmax["Softmax attention"]
        out["Attention output<br/>softmax @ V"]
        to_out["Project to dim"]
    end
    
    subgraph Residual["Residual Connection"]
        gated["Gated Residual<br/>learnable mixing"]
    end
    
    nodes --> to_q
    nodes --> to_kv
    edges --> edge_kv
    to_q --> sim
    to_kv --> add
    edge_kv --> add
    add --> sim
    sim --> mask
    mask --> softmax
    softmax --> out
    out --> to_out
    to_out --> gated
    nodes --> gated
    gated --> next["Output Nodes"]
    
    edges -.-> parallel["Passed through"]
    
    style nodes fill:#e1f5ff
    style edges fill:#fff4e1
    style gated fill:#e8f5e9
```

The key architectural components include:

- **Attention Layer**: Implements multi-head attention with dimension `dim_head` (default 64), configurable number of heads (default 8), and optional edge dimension [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L70-L106). The similarity computation uses scaled dot-product: `sim = q @ k / sqrt(dim_head)` with edge augmentation [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L135-L144).

- **PreNorm Wrapper**: Applies layer normalization before the function computation rather than after, which stabilizes training in deep networks [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L14-L30).

- **GatedResidual**: Implements a learnable residual connection that weights the contribution of the input and the residual using a learned gate computed from the concatenation of the input, residual, and their difference [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L50-L62).

- **FeedForward Block**: Optional two-layer MLP with GELU activation, configurable via the `with_feedforwards` parameter [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L179-L185).

> [!TIP]
> The gated residual connection is particularly important for graph transformers operating on biological sequences. By learning to dynamically balance new information against existing representations, the model can prevent catastrophic forgetting during training and maintain stable gradients through deep stacks.

## Triangle Multiplicative Module

The TriangleMultiplicativeModule implements edge-to-edge attention, a mechanism critical for capturing triadic relationships in residue graphs. Unlike standard attention which operates node-to-node, this module updates each edge representation by aggregating information from all edges that share a common node [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L12-L109).

The module supports two mixing modes controlled by the `mix` parameter:

- **'outgoing'**: For edge (i,j), aggregates over all edges (j,k) — focuses on residue j's outgoing connections
- **'ingoing'**: For edge (i,j), aggregates over all edges (k,i) — focuses on residue i's incoming connections [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L54-L57)

The operation uses a batched einsum expression: for outgoing mode `'... i k d, ... j k d -> ... i j d'` and for ingoing mode `'... k j d, ... k i d -> ... i j d'` [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L54-L57). This effectively performs a matrix multiplication along the shared dimension (the central node of the triangle).

The module incorporates three learned gating mechanisms initialized to identity functions:

- **Left Gate**: Modulates the left projection input [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L41-L42)
- **Right Gate**: Modulates the right projection input [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L43-L44)
- **Output Gate**: Modulates the final aggregated output [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L46-L47)

The complete forward pass includes layer normalization, projection through separate linear layers, sigmoid gating, triadic aggregation via einsum, final normalization and projection, and output gating [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L76-L109).

This module is inspired by the triangle multiplicative update mechanism from AlphaFold2, which proved essential for capturing residue-residue interaction patterns in protein structure prediction.

## Triangle Graph Transformer

The TriangleGraphTransformer serves as the primary integration point, combining the GraphTransformer and TriangleMultiplicativeModule into a unified architecture that updates both node and edge representations simultaneously [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L8-L63).

Each layer in the stack consists of three components applied sequentially:

1. **GraphTransformer**: Updates node representations using edge-aware attention [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L14-L23)
2. **Outgoing Triangle Update**: Updates edge representations using outgoing triangle multiplicative aggregation [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L24-L28)
3. **Ingoing Triangle Update**: Updates edge representations using ingoing triangle multiplicative aggregation [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L29-L33)

The forward pass iterates through each layer, applying the three operations in sequence. Edge updates use additive residual connections, allowing information to accumulate across layers [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L45-L56). Masking is applied symmetrically to edge representations using the pairwise mask derived from node masks: `tri_mask = mask.unsqueeze(-2) & mask.unsqueeze(-1)` [TriangleGraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleGraphTransformer.py#L51-L52].

The following table summarizes the key parameters and their default values:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `dim` | int | - | Dimension of node representations |
| `edge_dim` | int | - | Dimension of edge representations |
| `depth` | int | - | Number of TriangleGraphTransformer layers to stack |
| `gt_depth` | int | 1 | Number of GraphTransformer layers per TriangleGraphTransformer layer |
| `gt_dim_head` | int | 32 | Dimension per attention head in GraphTransformer |
| `gt_heads` | int | 8 | Number of attention heads in GraphTransformer |
| `tri_dim_hidden` | int | `2 * edge_dim` | Hidden dimension for triangle projections |

## Integration in IgFold Architecture

In the complete IgFold model, the TriangleGraphTransformer serves as the central feature extraction component, positioned between initial BERT embedding processing and subsequent structure prediction stages [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L53-L68).

The data flow follows this pattern:

1. **Input Transformation**: BERT features (512-dim) and attention maps (64-dim) are transformed to the model's node dimension through sequential linear layers [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L41-L52)

2. **Main Block Processing**: The TriangleGraphTransformer processes the transformed nodes and edges, producing refined representations that capture both local and long-range sequence relationships [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L242-L246)

3. **Template IPA Integration**: The refined node representations, along with pairwise edge representations, are passed to an IPA encoder that incorporates template structure information via quaternions and translations [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L247-L252)

4. **Structure IPA Prediction**: The structure-specific IPA transformer predicts atomic coordinates directly from the graph transformer outputs, using the same edge representations for pairwise attention [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L253-L259)

5. **Deviation Prediction**: A parallel pathway predicts local coordinate deviations for uncertainty estimation, using detached coordinates to prevent gradient interference [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L261-L270)

The architecture creates a powerful pipeline where graph transformers extract structural features that guide both template integration and de novo structure prediction. The edge representations computed by the triangle module serve as a unified pairwise encoding that propagates through all subsequent IPA stages.

> [!TIP]
> The hierarchical design—transforming BERT embeddings through graph transformers before passing to IPA—creates a natural separation of concerns. The graph transformers specialize in extracting sequence-structure relationships from the language model embeddings, while IPA specializes in geometric transformations. This modularity allows each component to focus on what it does best while sharing information through the edge representations.

## Component Interaction Patterns

The graph transformer components exhibit several key interaction patterns that enable effective antibody structure prediction:

**Node-Edge Coevolution**: Unlike standard architectures that process nodes and edges independently, TriangleGraphTransformer explicitly models their interdependence. Each node update depends on current edge information through edge-augmented attention, while each edge update depends on current node information through the projections used in triangle multiplicative updates.

**Progressive Refinement**: The multi-layer stacking (controlled by `depth`) allows progressive refinement of representations. Early layers capture local interactions (neighboring residues), while deeper layers integrate information across the full sequence length through repeated attention and aggregation steps.

**Gated Information Flow**: Three different gating mechanisms control information propagation:
- GatedResidual in GraphTransformer [GraphTransformer.py](igfold/model/components/GraphTransformer.py#L50-L62)
- Output gates in TriangleMultiplicativeModule [TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py](igfold/model/components/TriangleMultiplicativeModule.py#L46-L47)
- Post-norm patterns in IPABlock (used in subsequent stages) [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L238-L248]

These gates allow the model to learn when to incorporate new information versus preserving existing representations, a critical capability for handling variable-length antibody sequences with diverse CDR loop configurations.

The graph transformer components thus provide a robust foundation for extracting structure-relevant features from sequence embeddings, enabling accurate antibody structure prediction through careful design of node and edge representations and their interactions.

# Invariant Point Attention (IPA) Implementation



Invariant Point Attention represents a **geometric deep learning breakthrough** designed specifically for protein structure prediction, enabling the model to reason about 3D spatial relationships while maintaining SE(3) invariance—the mathematical property of being unchanged by rotations and translations in 3D space. This documentation explores IgFold's IPA implementation, which adapts the original AlphaFold2 architecture for antibody-specific structure prediction tasks.

## Architectural Foundation

The IPA implementation in IgFold consists of four hierarchical components that work together to process sequence information, template structures, and pairwise relationships into accurate 3D coordinate predictions. The core attention mechanism operates through two complementary pathways: a **scalar attention pathway** for sequence-level information and a **point attention pathway** for geometric relationships between atoms in 3D space.

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L34-L248), [IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py#L16-L175)

```mermaid
graph TB
    A[Input Representations] --> B[IPAEncoder]
    A --> C[IPATransformer]
    
    subgraph B ["IPAEncoder - Fixed Frame"]
        B1[IPABlock Layer 1] --> B2[IPABlock Layer 2]
        B2 --> B3[IPABlock Layer N]
        B3 --> B4[Updated Single Representations]
    end
    
    subgraph C ["IPATransformer - Evolving Frame"]
        C1[IPABlock Layer 1] --> C2[Quaternion/Translation Update]
        C2 --> C3[IPABlock Layer 2]
        C3 --> C4[Quaternion/Translation Update]
        C4 --> C5[IPABlock Layer N]
        C5 --> C6[Quaternion/Translation Update]
        C6 --> C7[Generate 3D Coordinates]
    end
    
    B --> D[Template-Aware Features]
    C --> E[Structure Predictions]
    
    F[Pairwise Edge Representations] --> B
    F --> C
    
    G[Rotations & Translations] --> B
    G --> C
```

## Invariant Point Attention Core Mechanism

The `InvariantPointAttention` class implements a multi-modal attention mechanism that simultaneously processes three types of information: scalar representations from protein sequences, point representations from 3D coordinates, and pairwise representations encoding residue-residue relationships. This design enables the model to leverage **sequence-structure synergy**—learning patterns that connect amino acid sequences with their 3D conformations.

The mechanism begins by projecting input representations into queries, keys, and values for both scalar and point attention pathways. For scalar attention, standard linear projections create `q_scalar`, `k_scalar`, and `v_scalar` with dimension `scalar_key_dim * heads` for queries/keys and `scalar_value_dim * heads` for values. For point attention, each head projects to `point_key_dim * heads * 3` dimensions, where the factor of 3 accounts for the three spatial coordinates (x, y, z).

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L34-L101)

### Frame Transformation and Point Attention

A critical innovation in IPA is the **transformation of local point representations to a global frame** before computing attention. Each residue maintains a local coordinate frame defined by its current rotation matrix and translation vector. The queries, keys, and values for point attention are first rotated into this global frame using einsum operations: `q_point = einsum('b n d c, b n c r -> b n d r', q_point, rotations) + translations`. This transformation ensures that attention computed in the global frame remains **invariant to local frame rotations**, as all points are expressed in a consistent coordinate system.

Point attention logits are derived from the squared Euclidean distance between transformed query and key points: `point_dist = (point_qk_diff ** 2).sum(dim = -2)`, where `point_qk_diff = rearrange(q_point, 'b i d c -> b i () d c') - rearrange(k_point, 'b j d c -> b () j d c')`. The attention mechanism learns a set of per-head weights that scale these distance measurements, enabling different attention heads to focus on different spatial scales. The final point attention logits incorporate these learned weights: `attn_logits_points = -0.5 * (point_dist * point_weights * self.point_attn_logits_scale).sum(dim = -1)`.

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L119-L145)

> [!TIP]
> The point attention mechanism's negative distance formulation means that attention weights decay exponentially with distance, creating a locality bias similar to convolution operations but with adaptive, learned receptive fields determined by the point_weights parameters.

### Attention Aggregation and Local Frame Recovery

After computing attention weights from the sum of scalar, point, and pairwise logits, the aggregation process diverges for scalar and point values. Scalar values are aggregated using standard attention-weighted summation: `results_scalar = einsum('b i j, b j d -> b i d', attn, v_scalar)`. Point values require a more sophisticated approach: they are first aggregated in the global frame, then **transformed back to local frames** to maintain consistency across attention layers.

The local frame recovery step applies the inverse transformation: `results_points = einsum('b n d c, b n c r -> b n d r', results_points - translations, rotations.transpose(-1, -2))`. By subtracting translations first, then applying the transpose of the rotation matrix, the aggregated points are expressed relative to each residue's local coordinate frame. The model also computes the norm of these local frame points: `results_points_norm = torch.sqrt(torch.square(results_points).sum(dim=-1) + eps)`, providing a scalar measure of spatial extent that contributes to the final output.

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L147-L192)

| **Attention Component** | **Input Dimension** | **Output Dimension** | **Role** |
|------------------------|---------------------|----------------------|----------|
| Scalar QKV | `dim` | `scalar_key_dim/value_dim * heads` | Sequence-based attention patterns |
| Point QKV | `dim` | `point_key_dim/value_dim * heads * 3` | Spatial relationships in 3D |
| Pairwise Bias | `pairwise_repr_dim` | `heads` | Residue-residue edge information |
| Combined Output | `heads * (scalar + pairwise + point * 4)` | `dim` | Integrated representation |

## IPABlock: Transformer Layer with Geometric Awareness

The `IPABlock` class packages the InvariantPointAttention mechanism into a complete transformer layer following the pre-norm/post-norm conventions established in the transformer literature. Each block consists of an attention sub-layer and a feedforward sub-layer, each with its own LayerNorm and residual connection. IgFold implements **post-layer normalization** as the default, matching the original AlphaFold2 architecture, but also provides pre-norm as an alternative for training stability.

The feedforward network employs a **three-layer architecture** with configurable hidden dimension expansion: `FeedForward(dim, mult = ff_mult, num_layers = ff_num_layers)`. This design provides more capacity than the standard two-layer feedforward networks in vanilla transformers, enabling the model to learn more complex transformations of the learned representations. Each layer includes a ReLU activation except for the final layer, which projects directly to the output dimension.

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L200-L248)

### Pre-norm vs Post-norm Architectures

The normalization strategy fundamentally affects gradient flow and training dynamics. In post-norm architecture (default), the normalization is applied after the residual connection: `x = self.attn(attn_input, **kwargs) + x; x = self.attn_norm(x) if post_norm else x`. This matches the original transformer paper but can lead to vanishing gradients in very deep networks. Pre-norm architecture applies normalization before the attention operation: `attn_input = x if post_norm else self.attn_norm(x)`, which generally provides better gradient flow for deeper networks but may require careful tuning of learning rates.

Sources: [IPABlock.py](igfold/model/components/IPABlock.py#L219-L248)

## IPAEncoder and IPATransformer: Hierarchical Processing

The implementation provides two higher-level abstractions for different use cases. `IPAEncoder` maintains **fixed coordinate frames** throughout processing, making it suitable for template integration and deviation prediction where the coordinate frame should remain stable. In contrast, `IPATransformer` progressively updates rotation and translation parameters through the network depth, enabling **iterative refinement** of predicted structures.

Both architectures share the same underlying IPABlock components but differ in how they handle coordinate frames. The encoder simply propagates representations through multiple IPABlocks without modifying the geometric parameters, while the transformer interleaves attention with frame updates to gradually improve coordinate predictions.

Sources: [IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py#L16-L54)

### Iterative Frame Updates in IPATransformer

The `IPATransformer` implements an elegant mechanism for updating coordinate frames using the learned representations. After each IPABlock, a linear layer predicts updates to both quaternions (4D rotation representations) and translation vectors (3D): `quaternion_update, translation_update = to_update(x).chunk(2, dim = -1)`. The quaternion update is padded with a constant 1.0 in the first dimension to maintain unit quaternion constraint: `quaternion_update = F.pad(quaternion_update, (1, 0), value = 1.)`.

The quaternion update is applied through quaternion multiplication: `quaternions = quaternion_multiply(quaternions, quaternion_update)`, which composes the current rotation with the predicted incremental rotation. Translation updates are rotated into the current frame before being added to the translations: `translations = translations + einsum('b n c, b n c r -> b n r', translation_update, rotations)`. This ensures that translation updates are expressed in the correct coordinate frame.

Sources: [IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py#L55-L145)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Input as Input Representations
    participant IPA as IPABlock
    participant Linear as Frame Update Layer
    participant QM as Quaternion Multiply
    participant Rotate as Rotation Apply
    
    Input->>IPA: Single representations + pairwise edges + current frame
    
    activate IPA
    IPA->>IPA: Scalar attention
    IPA->>IPA: Point attention
    IPA->>IPA: Pairwise attention
    IPA-->>Input: Updated representations
    deactivate IPA
    
    Input->>Linear: Updated representations
    
    activate Linear
    Linear->>Linear: Predict quaternion update (3D)
    Linear->>Linear: Pad with 1.0 (→ 4D unit quaternion)
    Linear->>Linear: Predict translation update (3D)
    Linear-->>QM: Quaternion update
    Linear-->>Rotate: Translation update
    deactivate Linear
    
    QM->>QM: q_new = q_current × q_update
    QM-->>Rotate: Updated quaternions
    
    Rotate->>Rotate: t_update_rotated = R_current × t_update
    Rotate->>Rotate: t_new = t_current + t_update_rotated
    Rotate-->>Input: Updated frame (R, t)
    
    Input->>IPA: Next iteration with updated frame
```

> [!TIP]
> The quaternion-based rotation updates maintain the SO(3) manifold constraint naturally, as quaternion multiplication of unit quaternions always produces unit quaternions, avoiding the numerical instability issues that can arise with direct rotation matrix parameterization.

## Coordinate Generation from Ideal Frames

The IPATransformer's final step converts learned quaternions and translations into atomic coordinates using an **idealized backbone template**. The `get_ideal_coords()` function defines a canonical backbone conformation with N, CA, C, and CB atoms at idealized positions based on average protein geometry. These coordinates are then repeated for each residue in each batch, creating a template of shape `(batch_size, seq_len, 4, 3)`.

The final coordinate generation applies the learned transformations to these ideal coordinates. First, quaternions are converted to rotation matrices using the `quaternion_to_matrix()` function, which implements the standard quaternion-to-rotation-matrix conversion. Then the ideal coordinates are transformed using batched matrix multiplication: `points_global = einsum('b n a c, b n c d -> b n a d', ideal_coords, rotations) + rearrange(translations, "b l d -> b l () d")`. This operation applies the rotation to each atom's coordinates, then adds the translation, moving the entire residue's local frame to its predicted global position.

Sources: [IPATransformer.py](igfold/model/components/IPATransformer.py#L146-L175), [coordinates.py](igfold/utils/coordinates.py#L33-L56)

### Oxygen Atom Placement

After generating the backbone coordinates, the model places oxygen atoms using the `place_o_coords()` function. This function computes the oxygen atom position using internal coordinates (bond length, angle, and dihedral) relative to the backbone atoms. The implementation uses the `place_fourth_atom()` function, which constructs a local coordinate frame from three atoms and places the fourth atom using specified internal coordinates. The oxygen is placed with a bond length of 1.231 Å, planar angle of 2.108 radians (approximately 121°), and dihedral angle of -3.142 radians (approximately -180°), creating the expected carbonyl geometry.

Sources: [coordinates.py](igfold/utils/coordinates.py#L57-L76)

## Integration in IgFold Architecture

IgFold employs three distinct IPA modules, each serving a specific purpose in the structure prediction pipeline. The **template IPA** (`self.template_ipa`) integrates template structure information into the sequence representations, using rotation and translation parameters derived from template coordinates. This enables the model to leverage known structural information while learning to predict accurate conformations for the target sequence.

The **structure IPA** (`self.structure_ipa`) performs the core coordinate prediction task, starting from scratch (identity rotations and zero translations) and iteratively refining the coordinate frames through multiple layers. This module generates the final 3D coordinates for all backbone atoms. The **deviation IPA** (`self.dev_ipa`) operates on the learned representations to predict per-residue RMSD scores, providing confidence estimates for the predicted structure.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L69-L112)

### Template Coordinate Frame Extraction

The template IPA requires initial rotation and translation parameters derived from template structures. The `get_coords_tran_rot()` method computes these parameters by aligning template backbone atoms to a standard frame. This involves computing the centroid of the template coordinates and extracting rotation matrices that align the template coordinates to an idealized frame. These frame parameters provide the geometric foundation for integrating template information into the IPA attention mechanism.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L114-L143)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Input ["Input Processing"]
        A[BERT Embeddings] --> B[Sequence Features]
        C[BERT Attention] --> D[Edge Features]
        E[Template Coords] --> F[Frame Extraction]
    end
    
    subgraph Graph ["Graph Transformer"]
        B --> G[Triangle Graph Transformer]
        D --> G
        G --> H[Updated Representations]
    end
    
    subgraph TemplateIPA ["Template IPA"]
        H --> I[Template IPA]
        D --> I
        F --> I
        I --> J[Template-Aware Features]
    end
    
    subgraph StructureIPA ["Structure IPA"]
        J --> K[Structure IPA]
        D --> K
        K --> L[Predicted Coordinates]
        K --> M[Rotations & Translations]
    end
    
    subgraph DevIPA ["Deviation IPA"]
        N[Deviation Features] --> O[Deviation IPA]
        D --> O
        M --> O
        O --> P[RMSD Predictions]
    end
    
    L --> Q[Final 3D Structure]
    P --> Q
```

## Configuration and Hyperparameters

The IPA modules are configured through a hierarchical parameter system that allows control over depth, head count, and attention dimensions. The configuration includes separate settings for each IPA module:

- `temp_ipa_depth`, `temp_ipa_heads`: Controls the template IPA's capacity
- `str_ipa_depth`, `str_ipa_heads`: Controls the structure IPA's capacity  
- `dev_ipa_depth`, `dev_ipa_heads`: Controls the deviation IPA's capacity

Each module uses the same underlying `node_dim` for the representation dimension, ensuring consistency across the architecture. The attention mechanism's internal dimensions (scalar and point key/value dimensions) use sensible defaults but can be customized if needed.

Sources: [IgFold.py](igfold/model/IgFold.py#L37-L48)

| **Module** | **Depth Parameter** | **Heads Parameter** | **Primary Function** |
|------------|---------------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Template IPA | `temp_ipa_depth` | `temp_ipa_heads` | Integrate template structural information |
| Structure IPA | `str_ipa_depth` | `str_ipa_heads` | Generate 3D coordinates from sequence |
| Deviation IPA | `dev_ipa_depth` | `dev_ipa_heads` | Predict per-residue confidence scores |

> [!TIP]
> The stop_rotation_grad parameter in IPATransformer allows detaching rotation gradients during training, which can improve stability by preventing large rotation updates from destabilizing the optimization process in early training stages.
